status: Independent prose corrections reconciled; not whole-source installation approval

corrected_fields.reason: Original initial i has a compact round dot. Adjacent īn and īm have detached flat macrons. Preserve this occurrence-specific short i.

Narrow original crop shows plain t with no detached underdot. The immediately following pāp kaktēn anlēn and standalone Kaktēn independently have plain t as well; correction is based on the phrase itself, not harmonization.

added_units.source_quote: The forms ending in r are properly plural forms.
added_units.source_caveat: Printed singular translations of aṇḍur and antēr remain unchanged; preserve the author’s morphological classification alongside their actual glosses.
added_units.reason: Explicitly identified bound morphology is not fully accounted by retaining only the whole-word examples.

source_context_requirements.claim: The same forms are usual in Kōlāmī.
source_context_requirements.disposition: Preserve comparative attribution in source-level commentary or the three control records; no invented extra Naiki forms.

source_context_requirements.claim: No materials for distinguishing long and short e and o; ōkō and irōṭēr are possible author readings.
source_context_requirements.disposition: Retain the qualification on proposed readings; no confident equivalence or phonological length claim.

source_context_requirements.claim: The dative and accusative do not appear to be distinguished.
source_context_requirements.disposition: Carry the tentative wording into final source commentary; pronoun-table case analysis inherits this qualified statement.

source_context_requirements.claim: Judged only from specimens, verbs apparently do not change for person; some counterexamples exist.
source_context_requirements.disposition: Preserve both statement and counterexamples. Do not force one person onto anlēn, or delete the source’s plural morphology analysis because English glosses are singular.

source_context_requirements.claim: The characteristic present consonant seems l; past t is also used in present or future tense.
source_context_requirements.disposition: Retain source tentativeness and all stated functions; do not classify t solely as a categorical past suffix.

source_context_requirements.claim: Kaktēn and similar forms are apparently nouns of agency.
source_context_requirements.disposition: Retain apparent status; whole I have done / I am one who did sin examples stay whole with their source translations.

source_context_requirements.claim: The source explicitly compares finite-tense, negative and infinitival constructions with Kōlāmī.
source_context_requirements.disposition: Preserve as source-level comparison; no unprinted comparative forms or etymology edges.
